chunks: Let him alone, O 'Ammar, for he has taken from religion only that which was close to his worldly gain, and he has willfully confused himself so as to make doubts an excuse for his shortcomings.
ai.seo_question: What was al-Mughirah's true motive for entering religion according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This narration highlights the political and spiritual nuance of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, whose conversion was viewed by Imam Ali as a strategic move for worldly gain rather than genuine conviction. The phrase 'deliberately confused himself' (al-bas) refers to his calculated ambiguity, allowing him to exploit religious doubts as an excuse for his lapses, a concept deeply analyzed in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the hypocrisy of early companions.
